column3: Ketenramm is pondering another problem.
Complete the critical encounter “Lost on the Wind” and obtain the Abductor's horn.
Deliver the Abductor's horn to the Archive.
What in the world happened to this isle during my centuries-spanning slumber?
I have nothing to add...
I ordered the crew to continue investigatin' aetherial currents in the area. While they're roamin' around, I thought we might consider the mystery from a fresh angle.

We've established that the Occult Crescent is a museum of sorts for the Fifth Astral Era, right? But here on the North Horn, these relics and ruins were deliberately meddled with, seemingly in the name of replicatin' later calamities. Why so?
Fortunately for us, there's someone right here who ought to know.
Iris, why don't you tell us a little about yer master?
As previously stated, I'm here to observe... Nothing more.
Heh. How about revisitin' a conversation we've already had, then? You wouldn't begrudge me that, would ye?
When we first met, I asked the Archive whether he'd summoned you. D'ye remember that?
Ye were adamant the “wizened little wretch” hadn't.
Were ye speakin' truthfully?
Indeed. That much was true.
“That much”? Hmmm...
In that case, it's fair to assume Iris's master is the ultimate source of wisdom on the isle: the architect.
Now, my understandin' is that a summoner and their familiar are usually bound by an aetherial flow. D'ye reckon we can leverage that to reach the tower somehow?
What will you say?
We ought to examine Iris more closely.
Iris isn't the only familiar, is she?
To conduct a thorough examination, I'm afraid we would need to reduce Iris to pure aether... She might be a bothersome little scapegrace, but I wouldn't wish that upon her.
I suggest we find and examine another of the architect's familiars─preferably one we'd have no qualms with vanquishing.
I suppose she isn't...
We came across a fair few familiars while roamin' down south. None of them particularly pleasant, mind.
I'm sure the North Horn has its own fair share of summoned creatures. Inspecting the aether of any one of them could further our investigation.
I might add that the denser their aether, the more information we stand to glean. Of course, such familiars tend to be rather more formidable...
Come to think of it, when I passed through the forest during our previous excursion, I spotted a large winged creature with a crest of green feathers. Perhaps you could seek them out?
I'm guessin' he means the wooded area north of the lake. Either way, sounds like a job for our resident fiend feller. Make sure ye hack off a chunk of them for us to examine, ye hear?
The trophy of which Ketenramm speaks can be obtained from a specific critical encounter in the forest to the north of the lake.
Speak with the expedition advisor should you wish to learn how to participate in critical encounters.
These big, dangerous fiends often control a swath of territory. Once yer there, it's just a matter of waitin' till they show up to hunt.
Don't forget to bring back a sample as Ketenramm requested. We shall need some physical remnant to examine the creature's aether, you see.
There are countless familiars besides me on this isle...
Felled the fiend, did ye? Best show the Archive whatever grisly trophy ye lopped off the poor bugger.
Pay me no heed.
Don't forget to bring back a sample as Ketenramm requested. We shall need some physical remnant to examine the creature's aether, you see.
Oh, what a handsome horn! Now, let us see what its aetheric signature reveals.
This trophy is wreathed in startlingly dense aether. The beast must have ranked highly among the architect's familiars. What was it doing when you found it?
The clearing was strewn with cages? I'd wager they were kidnappin' people and imprisonin' them in the forest.
That might explain why we never came across any survivors from those wrecks...
One thing is clear, though: the aether emanating from the horn bears a different signature to that of Iris.
I can't say for certain, but whoever called forth that creature didn't summon *her*.
Are ye suggestin' there's someone on the island besides the architect?
Or mayhap we're dealin' with multiple masters?
What do you think?
What will you say?
Perhaps stewardship of the isle changed hands?
The architect may have...transformed in the intervening centuries.
You already know this isle is home to knowledge most dangerous.
I sense that you may be capable of taking that knowledge beyond these shores.
Thus I ask you, what do you truly seek from your encounter with the architect?
What will you say?
I wish to see the isle function as a museum once more.
If he would use this knowledge indiscriminately, I intend to vanquish him.
Just as I expected... I have learned much about you during my quiet vigil.
In that case...
Forgive me... I have chosen to help the adventurer, regardless of my orders.
What are you talking about? Why apologize to me?
That head of yours really is devoid of all knowledge...
Before you assumed your current guise, it was *you* who summoned me.
